```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, dpi = 144)
```

A knitr document can show a plot as a static figure or an interactive viewer.
Quarto's R engine uses the same chunk options.

```{r plot, eval=FALSE}
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, z = hp)) + geom_point_3d() + coord_3d()
p
```

Set `view3d = TRUE` to embed the interactive viewer in HTML. PDF and Word
output draw the plot with the vector scene backend. The document's graphics
device determines the image format: for example, `dev = "pdf"` produces a
vector image for a PDF document. The viewer follows the chunk's `fig.width`
and `fig.height`, with its facet panels, titles and legends.

````markdown
```{r, view3d=TRUE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
p
```
````

In Quarto, the equivalent chunk begins with:

````markdown
```{r}
#| view3d: true
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
p
```
````

`alt_text_3d(p)` describes the layer types, mapped variables and camera
angles. This description supplies `fig.alt` for static figures and an
accessible name around an HTML viewer. Set `fig.alt` in the chunk or add
`labs(alt = "...")` to describe the finding in the plot.

```{r description}
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, z = hp)) + geom_point_3d() + coord_3d()
alt_text_3d(p)
```

Patchwork and cowplot preserve each panel's scene when arranging several
plots. Each scene is compiled at the physical dimensions of its panel.

When saving a raster scene, match the scene sampling resolution to the
output device. Both dpi values refer to the requested physical plot size.

```{r save, eval=FALSE}
raster <- p + coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("raster", dpi = 300))
ggsave("cars.png", raster, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```
